speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have multiple skin lesions; can you tell me how long they have been present and if they have changed in appearance or number recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Monkeypox (Mpox).

The presence of multiple painless, non-pruritic papules on the abdomen, combined with a recent exposure to a sibling with chickenpox and contact with a daycare peer with similar lesions, strongly suggests an orthopoxvirus infection despite the child being up-to-date on immunizations, which do not cover smallpox/monkeypox. I will proceed with confirming this via PCR testing.
